content: Nuclear respiratory factor 1 (NRF1), also referred to as Nrf1, Nrf-1, NRF1, or NRF-1, encodes a protein that forms homodimers and functions as a transcription factor. This transcription factor activates the expression of critical metabolic genes that regulate cellular growth, as well as nuclear genes essential for mitochondrial respiration, heme biosynthesis, and mitochondrial DNA transcription and replication. The NRF1 protein has also been implicated in the regulation of neurite outgrowth, which is a key process in the development and maintenance of neuronal networks. Alternative transcriptional splice variants encoding the same protein have been identified and characterized. Additionally, other variants encoding distinct protein isoforms have been described, although these have not been fully characterized. Confusion has arisen in bibliographic databases due to the shared symbol NRF1 being used for both this gene and nuclear factor (erythroid-derived 2)-like 1, which has the official symbol NFE2L1. NRF1 functions as a transcription factor that activates the expression of key metabolic genes involved in cellular growth and nuclear genes required for mitochondrial respiration, as well as mitochondrial DNA transcription and replication. Together with NRF2, NRF1 mediates biogenomic coordination between nuclear and mitochondrial genomes. It achieves this by directly regulating the expression of several nuclear-encoded electron transport chain (ETC) proteins and indirectly regulating the three mitochondrial-encoded cytochrome c oxidase (COX) subunit genes through the activation of mitochondrial transcription factors such as mtTFA, mtTFB1, and mtTFB2. NRF1 is also associated with the regulation of neurite outgrowth. Alternative transcriptional splice variants encoding the same protein have been characterized, while additional variants encoding different protein isoforms have been described but remain incompletely characterized. Cyclin D1-dependent kinase coordinates nuclear DNA synthesis and mitochondrial function by phosphorylating NRF1 at serine 47 (S47). NRF1 has been shown to interact with several proteins, including DYNL1 (dynein light chain 1), PPARGC1A (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha), and PPRC1 (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator-related protein 1).
